headline: 213 yards, a 50-yard answer, and a short week to Denver

sectionTitles.lastGame: Lumen Field film: 3-20 and no red-zone cash
sectionTitles.currentState: 5-1 with a thin skill room and a louder trade desk
sectionTitles.gamePlan: Denver at 3:25: take the early downs back
sectionTitles.pressConferences: Monday podium, still waiting on the official embeds

dek: Kansas City is 5-1 after Seattle won 20-3 at Lumen Field, and the next kickoff is at Denver on Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT on CBS with the Chiefs laying 1.5.
videoHook: Three points, 213 yards, and a division rematch that does not care how pretty the first five weeks looked.
theEdge: ESPN FPI still gives Kansas City 55.7 percent at Denver, DraftKings lists the Chiefs at minus 1.5 on a 41.5 total, and Polymarket sits at 10.1 percent to win the championship and 17.5 percent to win the AFC — a one-score favorite after a game the offense never controlled.

pressConferences.speaker: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, and Chris Jones
pressConferences.title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes & Chris Jones Postgame Press Conferences - NFL Week 7

storyline.lede: The 5-0 start met a Seattle team that kept the ball, ran it, and never let Patrick Mahomes find a rhythm. Kansas City finished with 11 first downs, 50 rushing yards on 16 attempts, 163 net passing yards, 213 total yards, and 24:09 of possession. Seattle finished with 24 first downs, 153 rushing yards on 41 attempts, 257 net passing yards, 410 total yards, and 35:51 of possession. Both clubs had eight drives and one turnover. The final was 3-20.
body: Seattle scored on a 25-yard field goal, a 28-yard touchdown, a 35-yard field goal, and a 21-yard touchdown. Kansas City’s scoring play was Harrison Butker’s 50-yard field goal. Butker also missed from 58 and from 45, and a late third-down throw to Travis Kelce ended in a turnover on downs. Mahomes was 19-of-33 for 165 yards with one interception, one sack, and a 58.3 rating. Seattle recorded seven quarterback hits. Kansas City recorded two. Sam Darnold was 20-of-28 with no sacks and a 96.9 rating.

Kenneth Walker III had 14 carries for 36 yards and four catches, 18 touches in a game Seattle clearly wanted to shrink. Emanuel Wilson had 24 rushes and one catch. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had nine catches and two rushes, including the 28-yard touchdown throw from Darnold. Drue Tranquill’s 12 tackles were the loudest Kansas City defensive line on the sheet, and the unit still could not get off the field: Seattle was 11-of-16 on third down, Kansas City 3-of-11.

Arrowhead Pride notes the defense still allows the second-fewest points per game in the league at 17.2, and that this was bend-don’t-break football that bent for too long. The same outlet’s power-rankings roundup has ESPN dropping the Chiefs from 2 to 4, with Kenneth Walker III listed as the best offseason addition even after a quiet rushing line.

Denver is next, and Arrowhead Pride already frames it as the louder question for a 5-1 team against a 5-2 Broncos club. Kansas City won the Week 1 meeting 31-10. This one is on the road, Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT, CBS. The market still leans Kansas City. The tape says the early-down run and the third-down stop have to show up before anyone treats that number as comfort.

lastGameReview.label: Week 7 · Sun, Oct 25 · 7:20 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Lumen Field, Seattle controlled both lines. Kansas City managed 213 yards and 24:09 of possession. Seattle managed 410 yards and 35:51 of possession. The visitors scored on Butker’s 50-yard field goal. Seattle scored 20.

analysis.body: The rushing gap is the film. Kansas City ran 16 times for 50 yards. Walker’s 14 carries gained 36, with Mahomes adding two scrambles. Seattle ran 41 times for 153. Wilson’s volume, George Holani’s six touches, Velus Jones Jr.’s five rushes, and three AJ Barner rushes — including direct snaps — kept Darnold in manageable down-and-distance. A second-quarter Wilson carry lost three to K. Tonga, and another lost a yard to George Karlaftis and Chris Roland-Wallace. Those wins did not change the down-and-distance trend.

Mahomes’ 19-of-33, 165-yard line included two 19-yard completions to Noah Gray, one deep right in the first quarter and one deep middle in the fourth, plus four Kelce catches for 44 yards and three Xavier Worthy targets that produced three catches and multiple incompletions, including a deep right with pressure from D. Hall and a deep left with pressure from M. Morris. The interception was a short left throw intended for J. Royals, taken by T. Okada with N. Emmanwori in on the play. Creed Humphrey’s first-quarter snap was fumbled and recovered by Mahomes. Hall later sacked Mahomes for a two-yard loss and forced a fumble that Mahomes also recovered. That is one sack and seven quarterback hits, not a clean pocket.

Seattle’s explosive answers were specific. Darnold’s deep left to Smith-Njigba was ruled a 27-yard catch to the 1, then reversed to a 28-yard touchdown. He had already scrambled left end for seven, and Jones had a right-end carry of 11. Later Darnold scrambled right end for 10. N. Williams intercepted a short middle throw intended for Rashid Shaheed and returned it 65 yards, with Karlaftis credited on the play. That takeaway did not produce points. Butker’s 58-yard try was short, and the 45-yard try was wide right.

Special teams and penalties framed empty drives. Kelce’s illegal shift wiped a first-quarter play. Kingsley Suamataia’s holding call wiped a fourth-quarter play. Seattle had three false starts, by G. Zabel, A. Bradford, and J. Sundell. On one first-quarter snap, J. Jones and O. Oluwatimi reported eligible before a direct snap to Barner up the middle. Later Barner direct snaps are on the log without that same report. Nick Bolton was injured on a third-quarter Wilson carry. The desk does not have a follow-up designation.

takeaways.title: Third down decided the clock
takeaways.body: Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs. Kansas City converted 3 of 11. Eight drives apiece, and Seattle held the ball for 35:51 to Kansas City’s 24:09. Spagnuolo’s group kept the score at 20, which matches the bend-don’t-break note from Arrowhead Pride, and still never stole a series.

takeaways.title: Walker never got a down-and-distance friend
takeaways.body: Eighteen touches, 14 of them carries, 36 rushing yards. Seattle’s front, not a mystery gap, is what the coaches have on film.

takeaways.title: The takeaways did not cash
takeaways.body: Williams’ interception was a real defensive play. It did not become points. Butker made the 50-yarder and missed from 58 and 45. A three-yard Kelce catch on fourth down turned the ball over on downs.

whatWorked: Gray’s two 19-yard catches gave Mahomes an intermediate answer when the deep shots to Worthy and Kelce were incomplete.
Williams’ interception and 65-yard return, with Karlaftis involved, was the defense’s cleanest event.
Tonga, Karlaftis, Bolton, and Tranquill each showed up on Seattle runs for negative or short yardage, and Tranquill finished with 12 tackles.
whatDidnt: Sixteen rushes, 50 yards, and 3-of-11 on third down left Mahomes in long-yardage shotgun too often.
Seven quarterback hits and one sack, plus Hall’s forced fumble on the sack, kept the timing offense late.
Two missed Butker tries and a failed fourth-down throw kept the only Kansas City points on the 50-yard make from changing the game.

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 5-1. The loss was the first of the regular season, and the national boards noticed: Arrowhead Pride’s Week 8 roundup has ESPN at 4, down from 2. The points-allowed figure through Week 7 is still 17.2, second-fewest in the league. The offense that just posted 11 first downs and 213 yards is the part that has to be rebuilt before Denver.

workOn.title: Early-down carries that are not heroic
workOn.body: Walker needs a carry count that is not stuck at 14 for 36. Denver will take the same invitation Seattle took if the first two downs stay behind the sticks.

workOn.title: Protect the 19-of-33 version of Mahomes
workOn.body: One sack and seven hits is the count. Suamataia’s holding flag and the Humphrey bobble are operational, not theoretical. Arrowhead Addict has already framed offensive tackle as a trade-market problem. Brett Veach does not have to complete a deal this week for the staff to change help rules and keep Gray and Kelce as defined answers.

workOn.title: Third-down stops without living on the takeaway
workOn.body: Seattle was 11-of-16. Kansas City had two quarterback hits. Cover-2 rally tackles and a called zone blitz are the install, not a claim that pressure created Williams’ interception.

thinkAbout.title: Is the receiver market a this-week problem?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Pride reports the club is calling around after failing to reach the red zone, with the Tyquan Thornton dislocated ankle already in the background of those talks. Worthy, Kelce, Gray, Justin Watson, Andrew Armstrong, Cyrus Allen, and Emmett Johnson are the catchers on this stat sheet. A deal is a front-office question. The Denver plan still has to be drawn from this room.

thinkAbout.title: How much did the snap sheet actually move?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict says the post-Seattle snap counts show trust shifting. Arrowhead Pride’s snap-count piece says L’Jarius Sneed had less playing time. Neither item hands this desk a full count, so the debate is about usage, not an invented percentage.

thinkAbout.title: Does 5-1 still own the division conversation?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict’s AFC West rankings piece argues the Chiefs still have the upper hand after Week 7. Arrowhead Pride’s community thread is louder because Denver is 5-2 and next. Both can be true until Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT.

gamePlan.lede: Week 8 is at Denver on Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT, CBS. Kansas City is a 1.5-point favorite with a 41.5 total. ESPN FPI has the Chiefs at 55.7 percent. The assignment is to look like the club that won the first meeting 31-10, not the club that just posted 50 rushing yards and 3-of-11 on third down.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Denver has already lost once in this building’s season story, 31-10 in Week 1, and arrives at 5-2 for a rematch the Arrowhead Pride community is treating as a measuring stick. Kansas City’s defensive points rate is still a strength. The mismatch risk is offensive: if Walker is stuck in second-and-long, Mahomes will see the same seven-hit profile Seattle just produced. Spagnuolo can live in Cover 2 and sprinkle simulated pressure. Bieniemy has to give him a lead, or at least a tied game, with inside zone and defined throws to Kelce and Gray.

keys.title: Make Denver defend 16-plus honest runs
keys.body: Sixteen attempts were not a run game. Script Walker under center and in shotgun on early downs, with Mahomes’ legs as a constraint, not the identity.

keys.title: Answer before the vertical
keys.body: Mesh and the screen are the answers to a rush that hunts. Four verticals can wait until Denver is light in the box. Worthy remains the outside vertical; he does not have to be the first read.

keys.title: Rally, then rush on your terms
keys.body: Two deep, five under takes away the shot that Smith-Njigba just cashed from another quarterback. The zone blitz is a call for a known third-and-medium, with a lineman dropping and a second-level rusher.

script: Open with under-center inside zone to Walker, then a Mahomes keep only if the edge widens.
Second series: mesh to Kelce and Gray, Worthy on the corner route, Walker as the checkdown.
If Denver shows a heavy rush on second-and-long, throw the screen and let the line get downhill in space.
Play-action boot off a successful inside-zone look, Mahomes to the perimeter, Gray as the flat answer.
Defensively, Cover 2 on early downs so Tranquill and Bolton, if available, can rally.
Call the zone blitz once on third-and-5 to third-and-7, drop a defensive lineman, and do not tell that story as a takeaway.

spotlight.tag: Run gap in the stat line
spotlight.title: Walker’s 18 touches did not move the line of scrimmage
spotlight.body: Fourteen carries, 36 yards, four catches. Team rushing was 50 on 16 attempts. Seattle’s 41 attempts and 153 yards are the contrast, and Denver will copy the down-and-distance if Kansas City allows it.

spotlight.title: One sack, seven hits, a 58.3 rating
spotlight.body: Mahomes was 19-of-33 for 165 with an interception. Hall forced the sack fumble. Mahomes recovered it, just as he recovered the Humphrey snap fumble. The count is the story. The adjective is not.

spotlight.title: 24:09 against 35:51
spotlight.body: Those clocks stay with the clubs on the box. Kansas City had the 24:09. Seattle had the 35:51, 24 first downs, and an 11-of-16 third-down line.

spotlight.title: Still laying 1.5 after a 3-20
spotlight.body: DraftKings has Kansas City minus 1.5 with a 41.5 total. FPI is at 55.7 percent. That is a lean, not a verdict, ahead of Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT.

spotlight.title: The phone is part of the week
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride says the Chiefs are calling around on a receiver. Arrowhead Addict has floated tackle targets while injuries cloud that spot. Veach’s deadline work and Bieniemy’s Sunday work are different jobs.

matchups.unit: Chiefs run game vs. Denver front
matchups.note: Walker was held to 36 yards on 14 carries in Seattle. The Chiefs rushed for 50. Denver does not get a free pass, but Kansas City has not earned the edge until the attempt count looks like the 27-carry, 150-yard prior game.
Seattle recorded seven quarterback hits and one sack. Mahomes’ rating was 58.3. Until protection rules change, the edge sits with the rush.

matchups.unit: Kelce and Gray vs. intermediate coverage
matchups.note: Kelce led the club with 4 catches for 44 yards. Gray had the two 19-yard gains on the log. That is the defined answer while the verticals stay incomplete.

matchups.chiefs: Steve Spagnuolo, Drue Tranquill, George Karlaftis
matchups.note: The Chiefs still allow 17.2 points per game, second-fewest, per Arrowhead Pride. Tranquill had 12 tackles. The Seattle third-down line is the warning, not a reason to hand Denver the unit edge.
Butker made a 50-yard field goal and missed from 58 and from 45. A 41.5 total means those kicks can decide a one-score game either way.

xsandos.title: Walker inside zone on first down
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 at Denver, before the down-and-distance gets Seattle-long
xsandos.why: Sixteen attempts and 50 yards cannot be the Week 8 identity. Walker’s 14-for-36 needs a zone path with a hat on the first second-level defender.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy: under center, zone steps, one cut. Walker presses the midline and bends only after the combo climbs. Mahomes is the constraint, not the carry.

xsandos.title: Kelce-Gray mesh vs. man
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 to 2nd-and-8, after a modest Walker gain
xsandos.why: Kelce’s four catches for 44 and Gray’s 19-yarders were the timing answers in a 19-of-33 game. Rubs give Mahomes a throw before a seventh-hit rush arrives.
xsandos.coaching: Kelce and Gray cross at five yards with a legal pick spacing. Worthy sits the corner. Walker is the outlet if the linebacker trails.

xsandos.title: Walker screen when the rush declares
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-long if Denver sells out up the field
xsandos.why: Seattle’s seven hits came when Kansas City was behind the sticks. A screen lets the line lead and gives Walker a touch that is not a stacked box carry.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes takes a hitch, not a hero ball. The tackle and guard release. Walker catches on the move and gets vertical only after the first block.

xsandos.title: Boot off the zone look
xsandos.situation: Play-action after two honest inside-zone carries have moved the line
xsandos.why: This is a Denver call, not a label on any Seattle throw. The boot moves the pocket after the run has been sold, which is how you keep a one-sack, seven-hit tape from repeating.
xsandos.coaching: Reid and Bieniemy: sell Walker, boot Mahomes to the boundary, Gray in the flat, Kelce bending into the void. Throw the flat if the edge chases.

xsandos.title: Cover 2 on Denver’s first down
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, two-deep shell, rally to the run
xsandos.why: Smith-Njigba’s 28-yard touchdown was a deep left shot. Cover 2 takes that window first and asks Tranquill’s tackling — 12 in Seattle — to finish the run.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo: corners sink, safeties stay on top, linebackers fit downhill. Karlaftis and Tonga hold the point so the second level is not tackling in the alley every snap.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz on third-and-medium
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 3rd-and-7, simulated pressure, no takeaway claim attached
xsandos.why: Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs while Kansas City managed two quarterback hits. The call is to show heat, drop a lineman, and rush a second-level player so Denver’s protection slides the wrong way.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo’s signature: declare a four-man look, drop the interior, and have the second-level rusher arrive after the protection sets. Tackle what you do not sack. Do not grade this card off Williams’ interception.

playmakers.name: George Karlaftis
playmakers.role: rushed or dropped on the call

coaching.detail: The prior game produced 422 yards, 22 first downs, and 30:26 of possession against the Chargers. This game produced 213, 11 first downs, and 24:09. The install is early-down honesty, not a new identity.

coaching.topic: Spagnuolo’s points rate vs. the third-down log
coaching.detail: Arrowhead Pride is right that 17.2 points per game is still elite. Seattle’s 11-of-16 and 35:51 say the shell has to tackle and get off the field, not just keep the scoreboard polite.

coaching.topic: Veach’s week is adjacent, not the call sheet
coaching.detail: Receiver calls and tackle-market pieces are on the wire. Sunday’s plan still names Kelce, Gray, Worthy, and Walker.

injuries.note: Arrowhead Pride ties the receiver-trade chatter to Thornton’s dislocated ankle and a red-zone-free loss.

injuries.status: Injured during play, no desk designation
injuries.note: The play-by-play says Bolton was injured on a third-quarter Emanuel Wilson carry. No follow-up status was supplied.

personnel.move: Sneed’s playing time dipped on the Week 7 sheet
personnel.detail: Arrowhead Pride’s snap-count analysis says L’Jarius Sneed had less playing time in the 20-3 loss. Usage, not a transaction.

personnel.move: Receiver and tackle markets are open conversations
personnel.detail: The club is reportedly calling around for a receiver, and separate pieces argue the tackle spot may need a deal while injuries cloud it.

personnel.move: Catch sheet from the Seattle game
personnel.detail: Kelce, Gray, and Worthy produced the receptions that moved the ball. Watson, Armstrong, Allen, and Johnson each appear on the touch list with one or two catches.

strategies: Script at least a Chargers-week attempt volume for Walker before asking Mahomes to play from second-and-long.
Use Gray and Kelce as the first answers; keep Worthy as the alert, not the required shot.
Boot only after the inside zone has been shown, so the fake is a real constraint.
Stay in Cover 2 on Denver’s early downs and rally with Tranquill.
Call one zone blitz on third-and-medium and grade it on the stop, not on a turnover.
Treat the 41.5 total as a field-position game: the 50-yard make counts, and the 58 and 45 misses are the reminder.
debates: Does a 1.5-point road favorite after 213 yards tell you more about Denver or about the market’s memory of Week 1?
Should Veach deal for a receiver before Bieniemy proves this catch sheet can move the ball?
Is Sneed’s reduced playing time a matchup note or a depth-chart note?
If Bolton’s in-game injury lingers, who is the rally linebacker next to Tranquill’s 12-tackle tape?
Is 17.2 points per game enough comfort when the other club just went 11-of-16 on third down?
